上海オフィスに赴任した渡辺さんと、中国の同僚・取引先との毎日。会議、会食、電話、: Daily life for Watanabe, newly posted to the Shanghai office, with Chinese colleagues and clients. Getting work done in meetings, at business dinners, on the phone and on WeChat.
上海オフィス初出勤: First day at the Shanghai office
東京本社から上海支社のマーケティング部に赴任した渡辺さん。月曜の朝九時、緊張しな: Makoto Watanabe has been transferred from the Tokyo head office to the marketing department of the Shanghai branch. At nine on Monday morning, he nervously walks into the office, and his boss, Ms. Zhou, gathers the department members. Everyone looks up from their computers at him. It's finally time to give the greeting he practiced back in Japan, in Chinese.
上海支社マーケティング部のマネージャー、三十代後半。仕事が早く率直、部下思い: Manager of the marketing department at the Shanghai branch, in her late thirties. Works fast, speaks frankly, and looks out for her team
東京本社から赴任した日本人社員、三十二歳。中国語は駐在前に一年集中して学んだ: A Japanese employee transferred from the Tokyo head office, 32. He studied Chinese intensively for a year before his posting
同じ部の若手社員、二十六歳。みんなから「小马」と呼ばれるムードメーカー: A young employee in the same department, 26. Everyone calls him 「小马」 (Xiao Ma); he's the one who keeps everyone's spirits up
周さんは渡辺さんの上司で、小马は同僚。中国の職場は日本より上下関係がフラットで、: Ms. Zhou is Watanabe's boss, and Xiao Ma is his coworker. Chinese workplaces tend to be less hierarchical than Japanese ones: people often use 「你」 rather than 「您」 even with bosses, and many companies have everyone call each other by name. Courtesy matters, but excessive self-deprecation isn't needed.
みなさん、ちょっと手を止めてください。紹介します。こちらは東京本社から来た渡辺誠: Everyone, stop for a moment. Let me introduce someone. This is Makoto Watanabe from the Tokyo head office. He'll be working in our marketing department from now on.
「介绍一下」の「一下」は動作を軽くする言葉。「市场部」はマーケティング部。中国企: The 「一下」 in 「介绍一下」 softens the action. 「市场部」 is the marketing department. Words like 「总部」 (head office), 「分公司」 (branch office) and 「部门」 (department) come up a lot at Chinese companies.
みなさん、こんにちは。渡辺誠です。渡辺と呼んでください。上海に来たばかりで、まだ: Hello, everyone. I'm Makoto Watanabe; just call me Watanabe. I've just arrived in Shanghai and there's a lot I'm still not familiar with, so I'd really appreciate your guidance.
「请多多指教」は改まった場面の「よろしくお願いします」。ここで日本式に「ご迷惑を: 「请多多指教」 is the formal "I look forward to working with you; please guide me." Avoid saying something like 「会给大家添麻烦」 ("I'm sure I'll cause you a lot of trouble"), as is customary in Japan; in China it sounds negative: "you're planning to cause trouble from day one?"
ようこそ！ 渡辺さん、中国語ペラペラじゃないですか。: Welcome, welcome! Watanabe, your Chinese is so fluent!
「溜」liū は「流暢な、ペラペラ」という口語。上海や北方の若い人がよく使います: 「溜」 (「liū」) is colloquial for "fluent, smooth." Young people in Shanghai and the north use it a lot. If you're complimented, just accept it with 「谢谢」.
ありがとうございます、まだまだです。これからわからないことがあったら、みなさんに: Thanks, but I still have a long way to go. If there's anything I don't understand, I'll be counting on all of you.
中国語の「麻烦」は「お手数をかける」という意味の動詞で、日本語の「面倒」より前向: In Chinese, 「麻烦」 is a verb meaning "to trouble someone," and it can be used more positively than "trouble" or "bother" in English. 「还要麻烦大家」 carries the nuance of "I'm counting on you," a way of showing respect for others.
遠慮しないで。あなたの席はこっちです。パソコンはもうセットアップしてあります。: Don't mention it. Your desk is over here, and your computer's already set up.
中国の職場では「姓＋役職」（周经理、王总、李主任）で呼ぶのが基本。「总」は社長や: At Chinese workplaces, the basic form of address is "surname + title" (「周经理」, 「王总」, 「李主任」). 「总」 is an honorific for company presidents and heads of divisions. At foreign companies and tech firms, though, people often use names or English names, so follow those around you.
周敏でいいですよ。うちの部はそういうの、あまり気にしないので。: Just call me Zhou Min. Our department doesn't stand on ceremony.
渡辺さん、WeChat追加してください。部のグループに招待しますね。: Watanabe, add me on WeChat. I'll pull you into the department group.
中国の職場では、日々の連絡や資料共有の多くがWeChatのグループ（工作群）で行: At Chinese workplaces, much of the daily communication and file sharing happens in WeChat groups (「工作群」). 「拉你进群」 = to add you to the group. Once you're in, posting a quick greeting like 「大家好，我是渡边，请多关照」 makes a good impression.
わかりました。ちなみに、普段の業務連絡はメールですか、それともWeChatですか: OK. By the way, for everyday work communication, do you use email or WeChat?
普通のことはグループで言えば大丈夫。正式な書類はメールで送ってください。: For ordinary things, just say it in the group. Send formal documents by email.
お昼、一緒に食べに行きません？ 下にめちゃくちゃおいしい麺の店があるんですよ。: Want to get lunch together? There's a really good noodle place downstairs.
ぜひ！ ちょうど近くにおいしい店があるか聞こうと思ってたんです。: Sure! I was just about to ask what's good to eat around here.
そうそう、明日の午前十時に週次ミーティングがあるから、日本側の状況をみんなに簡単: Oh, right. We have our weekly meeting at ten tomorrow morning. Could you give everyone a quick overview of how things are on the Japan side?
承知しました。今日中に準備しておきます。: No problem. I'll get it ready today.
中国の職場では、頼まれたことには「没问题」「好的」と前向きに即答するのが信頼につ: At Chinese workplaces, responding to requests positively and immediately with 「没问题」 or 「好的」 builds trust. A noncommittal "let me think about it" (「我考虑一下」) may be taken in China as "I don't want to," so be careful.
「东京总部」＝東京本社。支社は「分公司」、駐在員は「外派员工」: 「东京总部」 = Tokyo head office. A branch is 「分公司」, and an expat employee is 「外派员工」
営業部は「销售部」、人事部は「人事部」、総務は「行政部」: Sales is 「销售部」, human resources is 「人事部」, general affairs is 「行政部」
「还不熟悉」＝まだ慣れていない。「熟悉一下环境」＝環境に慣れる: 「还不熟悉」 = not used to it yet. 「熟悉一下环境」 = to get used to the surroundings
「请多多指教」は改まった自己紹介の締め。カジュアルなら「请多关照」: 「请多多指教」 closes a formal self-introduction. The casual version is 「请多关照」
「麻烦你了」＝お手数かけます。「还要麻烦大家」＝よろしく頼みます: 「麻烦你了」 = "Sorry to trouble you." 「还要麻烦大家」 = "I'll be counting on you all"
フリーアドレスでも「我的工位」と言う。職場の口語: Even with hot-desking, people say 「我的工位」. Workplace slang
「周经理」のように姓＋役職で呼ぶ。「总经理」は社長: Addressed as surname + title, as in 「周经理」. 「总经理」 is the general manager or president
w:讲究|こだわる、重んじる: to be particular about; to set store by
「不讲究这些」＝そういうのは気にしない。礼儀やマナーについてよく使う: 「不讲究这些」 = doesn't bother with that kind of thing. Often used about etiquette and manners
「工作群」＝仕事のグループ。「拉进群」＝グループに入れる: 「工作群」 = work group. 「拉进群」 = to add to a group
「发邮件」＝メールを送る。正式な連絡や添付資料はメールで: 「发邮件」 = to send an email. Formal communications and attachments go by email
「开会」＝会議をする。「例会」＝定例会: 「开会」 = to hold a meeting. 「例会」 = regular meeting
「介绍一下情况」＝状況を説明する。報告のキーワード: 「介绍一下情况」 = to explain the situation. A key word in reports
「我准备一下」＝準備しておきます。頼まれごとへの前向きな返事: 「我准备一下」 = "I'll get it ready." A positive response to a request
w:没问题|問題ない、任せて: no problem; leave it to me
頼まれたときの即答。自信と信頼を伝える: An immediate answer to a request. Conveys confidence and reliability
人を紹介するとき、商品やプランを説明するとき、ビジネスで最もよく使う言い方の一つ: One of the most common expressions in business, for introducing people and explaining products or plans. 「给」 shows who it's directed at. If you can open with 「我给大家介绍一下」 yourself, you'll naturally take the lead in meetings and negotiations.
ご紹介します。こちらが渡辺さんです。: Let me introduce someone: this is Watanabe.
弊社の新製品をご紹介いたします。: Allow me to introduce our new product.
このプロジェクトについて説明してもらえますか。: Could you walk me through this project?
……にお世話になります、……を頼りにしています: I'll be counting on...; I'll be relying on...
日本語の「ご迷惑をおかけします」に近い場面で使えますが、ニュアンスは「これからも: It's used in situations where some cultures would apologize in advance ("sorry for all the trouble I'll cause"), but the nuance is positive: "I'll keep relying on your help; thanks in advance." It doesn't put you down too much and shows you're counting on the other person, so at Chinese workplaces it's received far better than an apology.
これからもみなさんの力をお借りします。: I'll be counting on everyone's help from here on.
この件、引き続きフォローをお願いします。: I'll need you to keep following up on this.
会社のルールや習慣を説明するときの言い方。「再」は「その場合はまた〜する」。新し: A way of explaining company rules and customs. 「再」 means "in that case, do... instead." When checking how things work at a new workplace, ask 「一般用微信还是邮件？」; if you can catch an answer in this pattern, you'll grasp the rules right away.
普通のことはグループで、正式な書類はメールで。: Ordinary things go in the group; formal documents go by email.
普段は九時出社で、忙しいときは残業します。: We usually start at nine, and work overtime when it's busy.
初出勤、新しいプロジェクトへの参加、取引先への初訪問など、自分をチームに紹介する: Situations where you introduce yourself to a team, like your first day at work, joining a new project or visiting a client for the first time. Speaking briefly and cheerfully in the order name, what to call you, your enthusiasm, then 「请多多指教」 makes a good impression at Chinese workplaces too.
日本式に「ご迷惑をおかけします」「至らない点ばかりで」と自分を下げすぎると、自信: Putting yourself down too much, with lines like "I'm sure I'll cause you trouble" or "I have so many shortcomings," makes people think you lack confidence. And replying vaguely to a request with "I'll think about it" may be taken as a lack of motivation.
中国の同僚は、日本から来た人が溶け込もうとしているかをよく見ています。中国語で挨: Chinese coworkers watch closely to see whether someone from abroad is trying to fit in. Greeting them in Chinese, joining the group, saying yes when invited to lunch: each of these builds a sense of reassurance that "this person will be easy to work with."
日本の職場では謙遜と気遣いが美徳ですが、中国の職場では「自信」と「スピード」が信: In many workplaces, Japan's for instance, modesty and consideration are virtues, but at Chinese workplaces it's "confidence" and "speed" that build trust. When asked to do something, answer immediately with 「没问题」, and if you don't understand, ask right then with 「这个我不太明白」. Showing your weak points early and learning is valued far more than hiding them and failing later. Small exchanges, like having lunch together and sending each other stickers on WeChat, also build relationships where you can help each other when it counts. Ms. Zhou, who seems frank and strict, had his desk and computer ready in advance. People who notice that kind of thoughtfulness are trusted anywhere.
初出勤の自己紹介で、中国の職場でいちばん好印象なのは？: For a self-introduction on your first day, what makes the best impression at a Chinese workplace?
謙虚さは「还不熟悉」くらいで十分。最初から謝ったり迷惑をかけると言ったりするのは: Modesty along the lines of 「还不熟悉」 is enough. Apologizing from the start or saying you'll cause trouble sounds negative in China.
上司に明日の会議での発表を頼まれました。最も適切な返事は？: Your boss asks you to present at tomorrow's meeting. What's the most appropriate reply?
前向きな即答が中国の職場での信頼につながります。「考虑一下」は「やりたくない」と: A positive, immediate answer builds trust at Chinese workplaces. 「考虑一下」 may be taken as "I don't want to."
「我拉你进部门群」とは？: What does 「我拉你进部门群」 mean?
部署の会議室に連れて行く: I'll take you to the department meeting room.
部署のWeChatグループに招待する: I'll add you to the department's WeChat group.
部署の飲み会に誘う: I'll invite you to the department party.
部署の名簿に名前を書く: I'll write your name on the department roster.
「群」はWeChatのグループ。中国の職場では日常の連絡の多くがグループで行われ: 「群」 is a WeChat group. At Chinese workplaces, much daily communication happens in groups.
中国語の「麻烦」について正しいのは？: Which statement about 「麻烦」 in Chinese is correct?
「面倒くさい人」という悪口でしか使わない: It's used only as an insult, meaning "a pain-in-the-neck person."
「还要麻烦大家」は相手を頼りにしているという前向きな表現になる: 「还要麻烦大家」 is a positive expression showing you rely on others.
上司には絶対に使えない: You can never use it with your boss.
「麻烦」は「お手数をかける」という動詞としてよく使われ、「还要麻烦大家」は感じの: 「麻烦」 is often used as a verb meaning "to trouble someone," and 「还要麻烦大家」 makes a pleasant greeting.
